precepts.text: Talk no more so exceeding proudly; the Lord is a God of knowledge and by him actions are weighed. He raiseth up the poor out of the dust and lifteth the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes and make them inherit the throne of glory.
precepts.point: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh, the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee, thy tabernacle shall be in peace, and thou shalt not sin: Isaiah 60:21 says thy people shall be all righteous. Thy seed shall be great as the grass, and thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age like a shock of corn in its season: Israel's life will be long, forever.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
Job 5:11 says the Lord will “set up on high those that be low.” That is us: we are low right now, but he is going to set us up on high. And “those which mourn may be exalted to safety”: our people that mourn shall be exalted to safety and comfort. 1 Samuel 2 goes with it.

“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth.” The arrogancy is the foolishness, the teaching and the wisdom of this world. Pastor, don’t let that come out of your mouth. “For the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” He is going to judge all of us on our actions. Not your thoughts, though you must control your thoughts, but on what you do.

“The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength.” “The Lord killeth, and maketh alive”: it is the Lord that kills and the Lord that makes alive. “The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up.” That is what Job 5:11 just said: we are being brought low, but we are going to be exalted.

“He raiseth up the poor out of the dust.” The dust represents confusion, a low state of confusion, and the poor are the poor in spirit. “And lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill.” We are the beggar. Our people are begging for reparations, give us money; I want Section 8, I want a job, I want this. And the dunghill is this low place: whatever kind of house you have, compared to where we came from, it is a dunghill.

But he lifts them up “to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord’s, and he hath set the world upon them.” The Lord is going to make us inherit the throne of glory. That is the setting up on high of those that be low in Job 5:11.

precepts.text: We glory in tribulations, knowing that tribulation worketh patience, patience experience, and experience hope, and hope maketh not ashamed.
precepts.point: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh, the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee, thy tabernacle shall be in peace, and thou shalt not sin: Isaiah 60:21 says thy people shall be all righteous. Thy seed shall be great as the grass, and thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age like a shock of corn in its season: Israel's life will be long, forever.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
Job 5:17: “Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty.” We get corrected all the time. We might not be happy while we are going through it, but it says happy is the man whom God corrects. Romans 5 shows why.

“And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience.” There is a purpose behind tribulation: it works patience. “And patience, experience”: patience teaches you experience. “And experience, hope: And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts.”

That means we understand why God is allowing us to go through tribulation. He is teaching us something. While we are in it we might not understand it, but he is saying, I am trying to teach you a lesson here. That is why we do not despise the chastening of the Almighty.

precepts.text: Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. If ye be without chastisement, then are ye bastards, and not sons.
precepts.point: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh, the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee, thy tabernacle shall be in peace, and thou shalt not sin: Isaiah 60:21 says thy people shall be all righteous. Thy seed shall be great as the grass, and thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age like a shock of corn in its season: Israel's life will be long, forever.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
“For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth.” Whom the Lord loves, he chastises. This is why we go through things in our lives that we might not like at the moment. It is the same thing Job 5:17 says: “happy is the man whom God correcteth.”

“And scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.” So if you are in this truth, expect to get scourged. Expect to get beat.

“If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?” If you endure that chastisement, God is dealing with you like a son. “But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.” Nobody wants to be a bastard. So “despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty”: the chastening is the proof that you are his son.

precepts.text: Ah sinful nation, laden with iniquity; the whole head is sick, from the sole of the foot unto the head there is no soundness, but wounds, bruises and putrifying sores. Israel as a nation in Job's condition.
precepts.point: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh, the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee, thy tabernacle shall be in peace, and thou shalt not sin: Isaiah 60:21 says thy people shall be all righteous. Thy seed shall be great as the grass, and thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age like a shock of corn in its season: Israel's life will be long, forever.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
Job 5:18: “For he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.” He makes us sore, and Isaiah 1 shows where we are bruised from the top of our head.

“Ah sinful nation”: that is us, you and me. “A people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters”: we are the corrupters. “They have forsaken the Lord”: our people have forsaken the Lord. “They have provoked the Holy One of Israel unto anger, they are gone away backward”: we have gone backwards from God’s laws.

“Why should ye be stricken any more?” God is saying, I keep punishing you over and over, why should you be stricken any more? “Ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint. From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment.”

In Isaiah 1:4-6 he is talking about us in comparison with Job. Job was real, don’t get it wrong, but his life represents the nation of Israel. He lost everything, even his health, from the top of his head to the soles of his feet, and that is what Isaiah says about the nation of Israel as a whole. But the same God that “maketh sore” also “bindeth up”; “his hands make whole.” He will make us whole again.

precepts.text: The seventh angel sounded, and the kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord and of his Christ. In seven there shall no evil touch thee.
precepts.point: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh, the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee, thy tabernacle shall be in peace, and thou shalt not sin: Isaiah 60:21 says thy people shall be all righteous. Thy seed shall be great as the grass, and thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age like a shock of corn in its season: Israel's life will be long, forever.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
Job 5:19: “He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.” The six troubles mean the six trumps. And the seventh?

“And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever.”

So by the seventh trump there shall no evil touch us. It is going to be kingdom time. Then Job goes on: “In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword.” “Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue”: nobody is going to utter a word ever against the twelve tribes of Israel; you fix your lips to call us something, that’s off with your head. “Neither shalt thou be afraid of destruction when it cometh”: he is telling us not to be afraid when destruction comes, because it is going to come. Some don’t believe that because of America, God bless the USA, nothing could ever happen here. But it is coming, and the angels are going to protect the brothers and sisters that are alive at that time.

precepts.text: Thy people also shall be all righteous; they shall inherit the land for ever. A little one shall become a thousand: the Lord will bring certain spirits back quickly through marriage and childbearing.
precepts.point: At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh, the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee, thy tabernacle shall be in peace, and thou shalt not sin: Isaiah 60:21 says thy people shall be all righteous. Thy seed shall be great as the grass, and thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age like a shock of corn in its season: Israel's life will be long, forever.

note.label: Edom's Achilles' Heel

precepts.why:
Job 5:24: “And thou shalt know that thy tabernacle shall be in peace; and thou shalt visit thy habitation, and shalt not sin.” We won’t sin. Isaiah 60:21 says the same.

“Thy people also shall be all righteous”: our people shall be all righteous. “They shall inherit the land for ever”: we shall inherit the land forever. “The branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified”: we are the branch of God’s planting.

“A little one shall become a thousand, and a small one a strong nation: I the Lord will hasten it in his time.” We are going to have a whole lot of children. He is going to make sure to bring back certain spirits through marriage and childbearing; certain spirits are going to come back real quick.

That is Job 5:25-26: “thy seed shall be great, and thine offspring as the grass of the earth.” Our children are going to grow up quick. “Thou shalt come to thy grave in a full age, like as a shock of corn cometh in in his season.” Like a shock of corn comes back over and over, Israel is going to have a long, long life. That is why he calls it forever, eternal.

precepts.text: He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise; he taketh the wise in their own craftiness.
precepts.point: The gin shall take him by the heel, terrors shall make him afraid on every side, the missiles, and the firstborn of death shall devour his strength; Acts 26:23 says Christ is the first that should rise from the dead. He is brought to the king of terrors, brimstone is scattered on his habitation, his branch, his children, is cut off, his remembrance perishes from the earth, and he is driven from light into darkness and chased out of the world. Knowing Esau will be like a bad dream. Such are the dwellings of the wicked, him that knoweth not God.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
“The steps of his strength shall be straitened, and his own counsel shall cast him down. For he is cast into a net by his own feet, and he walketh upon a snare.” His own counsel casts him down.

Job 5 says the same: “He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise. He taketh the wise in their own craftiness: and the counsel of the froward is carried headlong.”

Remember it: crafty counsel. All of the things they did against us are crafty counsel. The way your neighborhood is set up, redlining, benign neglect, all of it; slavery, exploitation, colonization: all of it is crafty counsel. And God takes the wise in their own craftiness. The net Esau laid is the net his own feet are caught in, and his counsel is carried headlong.

That is how “the light of the wicked shall be put out”. And when Esau's light is put out, the black Christian's head comes right out of the white man's behind. That is the only way the Lord can separate you from the white man, because you are too far gone.

precepts.text: A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee.
precepts.point: He shall deliver thee in six troubles; yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee. Psalm 91:7 says a thousand shall fall at thy side and ten thousand at thy right hand, but it shall not come nigh thee. That fire is not coming near you.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
We read the judgment: the sword coming for Esau and for the nations, for the Lord “will give them that are wicked to the sword”. “But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.” Israel is the poor, and you escape that judgment by keeping the commandments with faith in the Lord and Saviour Jesus the Christ. “So the poor hath hope”: hope that something better is coming than what we are in right now.

“He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.” David shows what that looks like: “A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee.” That fire is not coming near you.

All that is read here is judgment: famine, war, the sword. “In famine he shall redeem thee from death: and in war from the power of the sword.” He is going to deliver you and redeem you from the power of that sword, even while thousands fall around you.

But it comes with correction: “happy is the man whom God correcteth”. Brothers get soft and mealy and yellow about correction, and sisters get bitter at those who correct them. Get rid of that soft spirit; man up and woman up. “he maketh sore, and bindeth up: he woundeth, and his hands make whole.” He wounds you with the word and makes you whole again, so that no evil touches you when the judgment falls.

precepts.text: The Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.
precepts.point: He saveth the poor from the sword. The poor are Israel.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
“He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, so that their hands cannot perform their enterprise. He taketh the wise in their own craftiness”. The crafty are the nations, in particular Esau, that counsel against us and keep exploiting, oppressing and colonizing with imperialism. It is the same as Psalms 21: “they imagined a mischievous device, which they are not able to perform.” Their counsel is carried headlong; they are going to fall headlong and bust their forehead. “They meet with darkness in the daytime, and grope in the noonday as in the night.”

“But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.” From Esau's sword, the nations' sword. Who is the poor? Isaiah answers: “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

Write it down, brothers: when the scripture talks about the poor, it is talking about Israel, the poor of his people who trust in Zion. That was an easy one, and every soldier should know it.

And before the Lord saves the poor from the sword, the wicked has to be identified. The man of sin must be revealed, so that the whole earth knows who he is: the nation that bombed country after country, removed leader after leader, and made the earth to tremble.

precepts.text: Call now, if there be any that will answer thee, and to which of the saints wilt thou turn; to learn the Bible you must go to one of the chosen.
precepts.point: He knows great is the wrath of the Lord poured out because the fathers had not kept the word of the Lord to do all that is written in the book. To inquire of the Lord, one must go to a saint, a chosen prophet who has the word.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
“Call now, if there be any that will answer thee; and to which of the saints wilt thou turn?” To inquire of the Lord, one must go to a saint, a chosen prophet who has the word. To learn the Bible you must go to one of the chosen.

That is what Josiah did. He had the book read before him, but he did not stop there: he “commanded Hilkiah, and Ahikam the son of Shaphan, and Abdon the son of Micah, and Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah a servant of the king’s, saying, Go, enquire of the Lord for me”, “concerning the words of the book that is found”. He turned to one who could answer.

precepts.text: The Lord founded Zion, and the poor of His people shall trust in it, identifying the poor as His chosen.
precepts.point: The poor of the Bible is the poor of His people, those that keep His laws, statutes, and commandments. So the poor have hope, and iniquity stops her mouth.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

precepts.why:
“But he saveth the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty.” Who is the poor? “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

The poor of the Bible is the poor of his people, those that keep his laws, statutes, and commandments, his chosen. The crafty meet with darkness in the daytime and grope in the noonday as in the night, walking in sin and darkness, but even though the heathen rage and their wrath comes at us to kill us, the Lord saves the poor. So the poor have hope, and iniquity stops her mouth.

precepts.text: Before affliction Job strayed, but the chastening turned him back to keep God's word.
precepts.point: He makes sore and binds up; He wounds and His hands make whole. The same hand that afflicts is the hand that heals.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

precepts.why:
“Behold, happy is the man whom God correcteth: therefore despise not thou the chastening of the Almighty”. This is a heavy truth: correction is a blessing, not a punishment unto death. “Before I was afflicted I went astray: but now have I kept thy word.”

Before affliction Job strayed, but the chastening turned him back to keep God's word. The Most High does not chasten us to kill us but to get us better, to show us the way he wants us to go and the instructions we can apply to our lives so we do not keep learning the same lessons over and over. He makes sore and binds up; the same hand that afflicts is the hand that heals.

precepts.text: It is good to have been afflicted, that one might learn God's statutes.
precepts.point: He makes sore and binds up; He wounds and His hands make whole. The same hand that afflicts is the hand that heals.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

precepts.why: “It is good for me that I have been afflicted; that I might learn thy statutes.” That is why happy is the man whom God corrects. The affliction is good because through it we learn his statutes, the instructions we can apply to our lives so we do not keep learning the same lessons over and over. He wounds, and his hands make whole: the same hand that afflicts is the hand that heals, and the man who learns his statutes from it is happy.

precepts.text: The seventh angel's sounding marks the finishing of the mystery, when it is time to be delivered out of this place.
precepts.point: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue, and not be afraid of destruction when it comes.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

precepts.why:
“He shall deliver thee in six troubles: yea, in seven there shall no evil touch thee.” The sixth points to the sixth angel and World War II. The seventh points to completion: “But in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he shall begin to sound, the mystery of God should be finished, as he hath declared to his servants the prophets.”

The seventh angel's sounding marks the finishing of the mystery, when it is time to be delivered out of this place, when the Most High takes his people off the earth. In seven there shall no evil touch thee. Deliverance comes by keeping the laws and commandments, and when you fall, getting back up through fasting, praying, charity, and forgiveness of your brothers and sisters, which are heavily important in these last days.

precepts.text: His servants who keep His commandments shall eat, drink, and rejoice, but those who refuse the truth shall be hungry, thirsty, and ashamed.
precepts.point: He shall visit his habitation and not sin. Peace and security come to the man the Most High keeps.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

precepts.why:
“At destruction and famine thou shalt laugh: neither shalt thou be afraid of the beasts of the earth.” The Lord shows who laughs at famine: “Therefore thus saith the Lord God, Behold, my servants shall eat, but ye shall be hungry: behold, my servants shall drink, but ye shall be thirsty: behold, my servants shall rejoice, but ye shall be ashamed”.

His servants who keep his commandments shall eat, drink, and rejoice, but those who refuse the truth shall be hungry, thirsty, and ashamed. The beasts of the earth point to the zoonosis of these days, Ebola, coronavirus, and the sicknesses created from splitting genes, and the righteous stay strong and steadfast in his truth. Peace and security come to the man the Most High keeps: his tabernacle is in peace, and he visits his habitation and does not sin.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

points: The crafty meet with darkness in the daytime and grope in the noonday as in the night; they walk in sin and darkness.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

points: But the Most High saves the poor from the sword, from their mouth, and from the hand of the mighty. Even though the heathen rage and their wrath comes at us to kill us, the Lord saves the poor.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

points: The poor of the Bible is the poor of His people, those that keep His laws, statutes, and commandments. So the poor have hope, and iniquity stops her mouth.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

points: Happy is the man whom God corrects; therefore despise not the chastening of the Almighty. This is a heavy truth: correction is a blessing, not a punishment unto death.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

points: He makes sore and binds up; He wounds and His hands make whole. The same hand that afflicts is the hand that heals.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

points: He shall deliver thee in six troubles, and in seven no evil shall touch thee. The sixth points to the sixth angel and World War II; the seventh points to completion, when the Most High takes His people off the earth.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

points: In famine He redeems from death, and in war from the power of the sword. note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

points: Thou shalt be hid from the scourge of the tongue, and not be afraid of destruction when it comes.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

points: At destruction and famine the righteous shall laugh, and not be afraid of the beasts of the earth. The beasts of the earth point to the zoonosis of these days, Ebola, coronavirus, and the sicknesses created from splitting genes. The righteous stay strong and steadfast in His truth.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

points: He shall be in league with the stones of the field, and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with him, and he shall know his tabernacle is in peace.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

points: He shall visit his habitation and not sin. Peace and security come to the man the Most High keeps.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

points: His seed shall be great and his offspring as the grass of the earth. He shall come to his grave in a full age, like a shock of corn gathered in its season.

note.label: Job 5: The Most High Corrects and Delivers His Righteous

points: Eliphaz closes: this we have searched out, so it is; hear it and know it for thy good. He presents his counsel as tested wisdom for Job to apply.
